description: We are Stellar Horizons, a NASA Space Apps 2026 team recognized with a Local Impact Award in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. We combine software engineering, data science, Earth observation, and environmental research to help communities prepare for floods and droughts. We welcome collaborators in hydrology, meteorology, geospatial analysis, and AI who share our vision of transforming rigorous science into practical solutions with global impact.
summary: What if the data we rely on to prepare for floods and droughts tell us different stories? In the Dominican Republic, we investigated 24 years of rainfall using NASA Earth observation data and other environmental sources, analyzing climate trends, their magnitude, and statistical significance. We uncovered a critical challenge: in 39% of cases where at least one rainfall product indicated drought, another reported normal or wetter conditions. We turned this discovery into Stellar Horizons, an intelligent environmental evidence platform designed to support flood and drought preparedness. It combines NASA observations, weather forecasts, watershed geography, and local environmental information to identify emerging concerns, investigate conflicting evidence, and guide preventive verification. Its evidence engine traces data dependencies, exposes uncertainty, and reassesses conclusions when supporting information changes. Starting with the Yuna River basin, we developed a reproducible approach connecting scientific investigation with community preparedness. Recognized with a Local Impact Award in Santo Domingo, Stellar Horizons began in the Dominican Republic with a global vision: helping communities worldwide make better-informed preparedness decisions through trustworthy Earth science.
details:
From Earth Observation to Community Preparedness

Floods and droughts threaten communities around the world, yet preparing for them requires more than collecting environmental data. It requires understanding what is changing, whether the evidence is reliable, and what should be verified before decisions are made.

Stellar Horizons is an environmental evidence intelligence platform developed in the Dominican Republic to support flood and drought preparedness. It combines NASA Earth observation data, independent environmental products, weather forecasts, watershed geography, and available ground observations.

How it works

Our system investigates 24 years of rainfall patterns across all 32 Dominican provinces, using 21 precipitation and drought indices. It evaluates where environmental conditions are changing, how quickly they are changing, and whether observed trends are statistically significant.

We apply scientific methods including Mann–Kendall trend testing, Theil–Sen slope estimation, autocorrelation adjustments, and multiple-testing corrections. Rather than relying on a single dataset, Stellar Horizons compares products and documents contradictions, uncertainty, and shared data dependencies.

Our scientific discovery

During our investigation, we found that environmental sources can produce substantially different interpretations of the same conditions. Among province-month cases in which at least one precipitation product identified drought, approximately 39% had another product reporting normal or wetter conditions.

This is not a measured failure rate of official warning systems. It demonstrates why environmental evidence requires careful verification before being used to support preparedness.

From science to practical action

Our four pilot territories are Bonao, Cotuí, Villa Riva, and Monte Cristi.

In the Yuna River basin, Stellar Horizons connects rainfall observations, forecasts, watershed geography, and historical flood evidence to organize preventive checks involving upstream conditions, river measurements, official notices, and potentially exposed communities.

For drought, it helps identify rainfall deficits and the additional information needed to assess water availability.

Its evidence engine tracks the origin, timing, and dependencies of information. When evidence changes or a source is removed, the system reassesses which conclusions remain supported. Users can inspect and export the underlying evidence.

Technology and innovation

The project uses Python for environmental data processing and statistical analysis, TypeScript and Vite for the web application, Leaflet and MapLibre for geospatial visualization, Observable Plot for scientific charts, and Docker for reproducible execution.

Our innovation is not simply visualizing climate data. It is connecting reproducible trend analysis, scientific cross-examination, and transparent evidence tracking with concrete preparedness workflows.

Impact and global potential

Stellar Horizons received a Local Impact Award at NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Santo Domingo.

Our goal is to help communities and local institutions investigate environmental signals and identify critical information before preparing for potential hazards.

The platform is currently a research and preparedness-support prototype, not a validated operational early-warning system. Its predictive performance and practical benefits require further testing.

Built around the needs of Dominican communities, Stellar Horizons is designed around a reproducible methodology that could be adapted to other watersheds, countries, and environmental challenges.

Our vision is to make trustworthy Earth science useful wherever communities need to prepare.
